correctness.rationale: For the published Eq. (1), the eight-dimensional infected linearization is F-V with new-entry states E_C,E_M,E_r and lower triangular V with positive diagonal a,b,c,d,e,u,g,h. Exact symbolic inversion and path accounting yield a three-by-three block-upper-triangular next-generation matrix, with a coupled two-by-two human block and rodent eigenvalue. Because V is a nonsingular M-matrix, the standard threshold theorem establishes local asymptotic stability for spectral radius less than one and instability for greater than one, without asserting either conclusion at equality. An exact rational parameter assignment satisfying strict positivity gives G=[[329/180,56/45,0],[8/45,47/180,1/4],[0,0,1/4]], corrected radius 47/45+sqrt(27049)/180>1 and separate published maximum 7/8<1. The standalone verify.py was executed from its packaged source path and returned VERIFY_OK. The proof neither relies on finite simulation as an infinite argument nor claims global dynamics.

value.rationale: The model was proposed to evaluate disease-control thresholds; reversing an explicit claimed local-stability verdict on an open set of strictly positive rates is consequential, unlike a cosmetic sign check. The positive cross-progression pathways in the actual published equations create a new direct reproduction route and two-way human invasion coupling. The exact coupled spectrum quantifies how and when separate-pathogen thresholds cease to represent the full model. It does not claim empirical epidemiological policy validity or global disease dynamics.
